title: Intent-driven client prioritization and staged degrade orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a coordinated, intent-aware load-shedding layer that combines client-declared intent tokens, budgeted request slimming, and a staged degrade orchestrator that works across regions and interacts cleanly with circuit breakers. Current admission logic is reactive and coarse: tenants get tripped wholesale or experience binary fallbacks. The goal is graceful, explainable degradation paths that preserve high-value intents and avoid cascading regional failovers while keeping SLOs (p99 latency and availability) within targets.

Motivation / Background:
- Incidents in Q4 showed tenants with mixed traffic patterns caused noisy neighbors to push healthy clients into hard fallbacks.
- Multi-region failover sometimes amplifies load due to duplicated retries when clients are unaware of partial degradation.
- We lack a first-class way for upstream services to express intent (e.g., interactive vs. background, high-fidelity vs. low-fidelity) that the runtime can use for differentiated admission.

High-level approach:
1) Intent token: extend request metadata to accept an optional intent label (e.g., "interactive", "background", "batch-preview", "billing-critical"). The runtime maps intents to priority buckets and per-intent budgets.
2) Budgeted slimming: per-tenant and per-intent request budgets that allow soft trimming (truncate max tokens, switch quantized model, disable non-essential features such as tool calls) before full rejection.
3) Staged degrade orchestrator: a finite state machine that implements ordered degradation steps (e.g., prefix caching preference -> token limit -> model downgrade -> partial response -> reject) with tunable thresholds. Steps are annotated with cost delta and estimated quality impact.
4) Circuit breaker integration: circuit breakers track per-region SLO health and feed signals into the orchestrator; when a breaker trips, orchestrator shifts to more aggressive stages only for affected region/availability zone and routes higher-priority intents to healthier regions if allowed.
5) Retry and client guidance: enrich 429 responses with structured metadata describing active degradation profile, expected retry-backoff, and recommended client behavior to avoid storming healthy regions.

Design details / APIs:
- New request header: X-Redwood-Intent (freeform token validated against allowed intents list). Fall back to "interactive" for unknown/absent intent.
- New config objects: IntentProfile(name, priorityWeight, defaultBudgetPerMinute, degradeSteps[]). Degrade steps are ordered strings (e.g., "trim_tokens", "quantize", "disable_tools", "partial_response", "reject").
- Admission flow: admission checks applied in order: tenant available budget -> region headroom -> intent priority -> predictive SLO score -> apply first available degrade step if budget exceeded.
- Metrics to emit: intent.request_count, intent.degrade_step_applied, intent.rejection_rate, intent.avg_latency_p50_p95_p99, intent.region_failover_count. All tags include tenant_id and region.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implementation can apply per-intent degrade steps without requiring per-tenant code changes.
- During a controlled chaos test (see runbook), top-2 intents maintain p99 latency < 350ms and availability > 99.5% while overall system CPU/GPU utilization hits 85% sustained.
- 429 responses for degraded requests include structured guidance and a link to console documentation.
- Circuit breaker interactions: when a region breaker trips, no more than 5% of active high-priority interactive intents are rejected; majority should be routed to fallback regions if capacity exists.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A: Feature flag behind runtime-1.22. Enable intent header parsing and metrics emission (no enforcement) for 1 week to build telemetry.
- Phase B: Soft enforcement for a small cohort of tenants (internal dev teams + 3 pilot customers). Monitor SLOs and iterate degrade step parameters for 2 weeks.
- Phase C: Incremental ramp to 25% of production load with automated rollback if SLO regressions > 1 percentage point.
- Phase D: Global enable with console controls for tenants to opt-in/out and set intent priority overrides.

Monitoring and alerting:
- New dashboards: Intent heatmap (requests by intent), Degrade waterfall (counts by step), Region failover funnel.
- Alerts: rapid spike in intent.degrade_step_applied for a high-priority intent (>10% increase in 5m), region failover rate > 1% sustained, unexpected rise in client retries after failure responses.

Security and compliance notes:
- Intent tokens are non-sensitive metadata; do not accept PII in the header. Document in API docs and validate on ingestion.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Default intent semantics: Should missing intent default to "background" (safer for resource isolation) or "interactive" (better UX)? Current proposal defaults to interactive to preserve existing behavior but logs anonymized counts for policy change discussions.
- Complexity vs. predictability: intent-weighted admission introduces more moving parts in scheduling; need clear observability and simple fallback defaults to avoid operational surprises.

Next steps / tasks (owner):
- Implement X-Redwood-Intent parsing and config schema (Marco) - PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/7892.
- Instrument metrics and dashboards (SRE team, owner: Priya Rao).
- Implement budgeted slimming primitives in admission controller (owner: Marco).
- Author canary runbook and chaos scenario (owner: Aisha).
- Console UI controls for intent profiles (PM/Frontend).

comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha: Initial spike analysis attached to the design doc. Found 3 tenants responsible for 40% of ephemeral load spikes; intent tagging could have prevented wholesale fallback.
2026-03-04 - Marco: Prototype of header parsing and intent->bucket mapping submitted. Basic metrics emitted to staging via prometheus.intent.*, see PR #7892.
2026-03-06 - Priya: Dashboard skeleton live in staging. Need to add percentiles and per-tenant drilldown. Alert thresholds proposed in the runbook.
2026-03-08 - Security review: Confirmed intent tokens are safe to log as non-sensitive. Recommend truncating freeform string to 64 chars for index stability.
2026-03-10 - Ops runbook comment: When routing intents across regions, prefer stale-tolerant requests to fallbacks to reduce retry storms. Added retry guidance to 429 payloads.
2026-03-12 - Marco: Began integration tests for staged degrade FSM. Discovered race condition when switching degrade steps under transient region pressure; mitigation in next patch.
